newsitem.title: EGYPT: Islamist gunmen kill policeman, farmer in Egypt.
newsitem.headline: Islamist gunmen kill policeman, farmer in Egypt.

text.p: Suspected Moslem militant gunmen shot dead a policeman and a farmer in a southern Egyptian town on Tuesday and then fled with an automatic rifle, security sources said.

They said the gunmen -- believed to be members of the militant Gama'a al-Islamiya (Islamic Group) waging a low-level guerilla war in the south -- killed policeman Ragab Mohamed Hassan while he was guarding gold shops in Minya province, some 240 km (150 miles) south of Cairo.
The gunmen seized the policeman's rifle, killed the farmer who was passing by and injured another resident before escaping. Police are searching the outskirts of the town, the sources said.

Since 1992, the Gama'a and other militant groups have been trying to transform Egypt into a strict Islamic state. They have often attacked goldsmiths and banks to fund activities, prompting officials to post extra security around them.
More than 1,000 people have been killed in the five years of political violence during which militants have also targetted Christians, tourists and officials.
